teaching.purpose: Maren hands over a mystery Lexling that arrived in a basket, and it picks you as its partner on the spot.

grounding.how: Maren says hello to Milo; Milo waves back at her, then turns and waves at you.

steps.text: The Translators' Lodge smells of old paper and woodsmoke. Lexlings chatter somewhere up in the rafters.
There you are. Welcome to the Lodge, Translator-in-training. I'm Maren.
Anyone can tell when a Lexling is happy or scared. A Translator learns what they want: food, water, come, go, danger. A handful of sounds. It takes years, and that's about as far as anyone gets.
Now. This arrived this morning. No letter. Just a tag.
The basket wiggles.
A small, round Lexling pops out, ears first.
Hello there, little one.
Ha! He's greeting us. They pick that up from people, you know.
He turns to you and waves again.
Milo bounces on the spot.
Milo trots around Maren's boots to find you.
Well, I'll be. He's chosen you. I've never seen a Lexling pick a partner that fast.
The tag says MILO. Found at the edge of Whisperwood. And I'll be honest: I don't know what kind of Lexling he is. I've never seen one like him.
Take these: a flask, some sunberries, a charm, and a good stick. Every adventurer needs a good stick. Your camp's down the hill. Get him settled, and Whisperwood is past it when you're ready.
And listen to him. Really listen. That's the whole job.

teaching.purpose: You report the Emberhog to Maren, who learns what Milo can do. Pip turns up sure he knows what his Puffkin wants.

steps.text: You're back! In one piece, too. Someone said an Emberhog came tearing through the ferns down by the stream.
You tell Maren everything: the stream, the Emberhog, and the four kinds of magic Milo was ready to throw at it. Water. Fire. Earth. Wind.
Four?
Lexlings have one element. One. Fire Lexlings breathe fire. Water Lexlings make water. That's how it has always been.
Milo scratches his ear, unbothered.
Whatever he is, let's keep it between us for now.
Maren! Bluster and I tracked that Emberhog halfway to the ridge! Oh. Hello. Pip Calloway, Translator Second Class.
Self-appointed.
Bluster and I understand each other perfectly. Five years together. Watch.
See that circling? He's restless. Wind Lexlings hate being cooped up indoors. He wants to go back out.

steps.prompt: Bluster drifts in slow circles over the snack bowl.

steps.text: Bluster snatches the berry out of the air.
Restless AND hungry. Obviously. That's what I meant.
Maren looks at you over her glasses for a long moment. Then she writes something in her notebook.
Pip opens the door. Bluster ignores it completely, drops into the snack bowl and starts eating.
Restless, was he?
Restless and hungry. It's called doing two things at once.
Keep your ears open out there, both of you. Lexlings have been restless all season, and I don't mean hungry. Something's stirring in Whisperwood.
End of Chapter One. Whisperwood is still out there, and so is whoever is looking for Milo.

teaching.purpose: Maren passes on a Translator's rule of thumb, and Milo agrees with it.

steps.text: A tip. When a Lexling makes the same sound twice, it usually really means it.
See?
Fire Lexlings hate getting wet. Don't tell them I told you.
And wind only makes a fire bigger. I learned that one the hard way.
If something big charges you, put something solid in its way. A rock, a wall, anything. Lexlings don't announce their charges, so you just have to be quick.
Milo tilts his head, as if that last part wasn't quite right.

teaching.purpose: Tea at the Lodge, and Milo makes sure nobody forgets about him.

steps.text: Sit, sit. The kettle's on.
That one I don't need explained. There are sunberries in the bowl.
Milo watches every berry go into your mouth.
Oh, give him one.
